claims.text: Amazon reported AWS sales up 37% to $42.2 billion and AWS operating income of $16.6 billion, versus $10.2 billion a year earlier.
The issuer says its $62.6 billion of quarterly net income includes $53.4 billion of nonoperating pretax other income, primarily from Anthropic investments. That amount is not operating profit.
claims.source_cue: non-operating pre-tax other income of $53.4 billion

claims.text: Amazon guided third-quarter 2026 net sales to $197–202 billion, or 9–12% year-on-year growth, with roughly 80 basis points of currency headwind. The issuer says growth excluding Prime Day's timing effect in both years would be nearly 400 basis points higher.

reads.question: How much of the earnings change reflects recurring operations, given the issuer-described nonoperating investment gain?

claims.text: Lilly attributed 48% year-on-year revenue growth to 60% higher volume, partly offset by a 13% decline in realized prices. Its issuer-defined Key Products basket reached $15.7 billion, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound.
claims.source_cue: driven by a 60% increase in volume

claims.text: Lilly says a $2.78 midpoint rise in underlying non-GAAP EPS guidance was more than offset by $3.03 of acquired in-process R&D charges, leaving updated full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance at $35.50–36.50. These are issuer-defined non-GAAP measures.
Lilly raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance from $82–85 billion to $85–87 billion. This is issuer guidance, not a realized result.

reads.question: Will the issuer's reported volume gains continue to outweigh lower realized pricing?

claims.text: Home Depot reported total sales up 5.7%, while comparable sales rose 1.7% and U.S. comparable sales rose 1.3%. The different growth rates should not be treated as the same measure.
claims.source_cue: Comparable sales for the second quarter

claims.text: The company reaffirmed fiscal-2026 guidance for roughly 2.5–4.5% total sales growth and flat-to-2% comparable sales growth. Its guidance assumes IEEPA tariff refunds partly offset higher input costs.

reads.question: What explains the gap between total-sales growth and comparable-sales growth, and is that mix durable?
